author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “Rostopchin baving been pronounced, I presumed to remark, that tbe colour at that time given to bis patriotic action, bad very much surprized me, for he bad interested me instead of exciting my indignation, and even much more, that I bad envied bim!. […]”
sourceTitle: Las Cases, Mémorial (English ed., 1823), Fifth Part conversations
archive: Las Cases, Journal of Napoleon's St Helena conversations (London, 1823) — public domain
context: On Moscow's burning and Rostopchin; undated conversation, 1816. Reported speech via Las Cases' journal; undated in print except where stated.

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “Abolit ten o'clock, the Emperor entered my apartment; lie came imawares, as he wished to take a walk. I followed him, and he walked for some time towards the wood, where \ve were taken up by the calash. A considérable interval had elapsed since he made use of it. […]”

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “I die prematurely, assassinated by the English oligarchy and its hired killer; the English people will soon avenge me. […]”
archive: Antommarchi, Derniers momens de Napoléon (Paris, 1825) — public domain (French)
context: Dictated mid-April 1821; widely printed within months. Date certain to the month; day approximate. Translated for Chronicle from the public-domain French; original below.
originalText: Je meurs prématurément, assassiné par l'oligarchie anglaise et son sicaire; le peuple anglais ne tardera pas à me venger.

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “I desire my ashes to rest on the banks of the Seine, amid the French people I loved so well. […]”
archive: Antommarchi, Derniers momens de Napoléon (Paris, 1825) — public domain (French)
context: Holograph codicil, sealed with his arms; the governor refused it. Same dating note as above. Translated for Chronicle from the public-domain French; original below.
originalText: Je désire que mes cendres reposent sur les bords de la Seine, au milieu de ce peuple français que j'ai tant aimé.

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “Tell them the great Napoleon expired in the most deplorable state, wanting everything, abandoned to himself and his glory. […]”
archive: Antommarchi, Derniers momens de Napoléon (Paris, 1825) — public domain (French)
context: Dictated to Antommarchi days before May 5; reported speech via the doctor's journal. Translated for Chronicle from the public-domain French; original below.
originalText: Vous leur direz que le grand Napoléon est expiré dans l'état le plus déplorable, manquant de tout, abandonné à lui-même et à sa gloire.
